events.headline: 'Abhorrent': UN condemns US plan to livestream execution of gunman who killed 13 at Texas military base i
events.text: According to The Times of India, the United Nations on Friday condemned US (United States - country in North America; world's largest economy) plans to livestream the execution of former US Army Major Nidal Hasan, who killed 13 people at the Fort Hood military base on November 5, 2009, calling the move "abhorrent" and warning that it could violate the prohibition against torture. "These kinds of public executions we've seen in other countries, whether it's Iran or Afghanistan ... can constitute a form of cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment, or punishment," UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric told a daily briefing at the UN headquarters in New York. "Showing it live is tantamount ... to it being public, and could be a violation of the prohibition against torture," he added. "A government executing someone in public, or in front of live cameras, frankly, is abhorrent." Hasan is scheduled to become the first person executed by a US military firing squad since 1945. events.headline: F-35 for India? 'US didn't even let Indian Air Force near it': IAF Chief's humorous response to US fighter jet offer
events.text: According to The Week, Indian Air Force (IAF) Chief Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh on Saturday took a humorous dig at the United States over its F-35 fifth-generation stealth fighter aircraft, saying that US Air Force personnel did not even allow Indian personnel near the jet. The remark came during a press conference on the sidelines of the concluding ceremony of the multinational air exercise Tarang Shakti-2026 in Jodhpur, where the US F-35 is participating for the first time. Sitting alongside the commander of the US Air Force's Pacific Air Forces (PACAF), Singh was asked about reports suggesting that the United States had offered the advanced fighter aircraft to India. "Your people don't even let us go near the aircraft, and you are talking about selling it to us," the IAF chief quipped. events.headline: Indian stock markets snap 8-week losing streak - What's next for Sensex, Nifty? Triggers, strategy ​for investors
events.text: According to Livemint, Indian equity markets ended their eight-week losing streak, the longest in 25 years, after a volatile (changing quickly and unpredictably) week in which benchmarks recovered on buying in information technology (IT), fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), automobile and financial stocks. However, persistent foreign fund outflows, elevated crude oil prices, rising global bond yields and uncertainty over the monetary policy outlook continued to weigh on investor sentiment. For the week, the BSE (Bombay Stock Exchange - Asia's oldest stock exchange; runs the Sensex) Sensex gained 562.63 points, or 0.78%, to close at 72,472.33, while the Nifty 50 advanced 98.5 points, or 0.43%, to settle at 22,520.45. The recovery gathered momentum on Friday, October 9, when the Sensex surged 879.09 points, or 1.23%, to 72,472.33. The Nifty 50 climbed 288.65 points, or 1.30%, to end at 22,520.45, snapping the benchmarks' eight-week losing streak. In related news, News18 reported: Market Today: Sensex Jumps 879 Points, Nifty Closes Above 22,500; IT, FMCG Stocks Lead Gains.

events.text: The Reserve Bank of India reported in its October Bulletin that the Indian economy remains resilient despite global uncertainty. This strength is driven by solid macroeconomic fundamentals, sustained domestic demand, and strong services. To manage risks, the RBI used policy interventions and regulatory measures to stop speculative activity in the foreign exchange market. These efforts, along with strong export growth, helped narrow the trade deficit (shortfall; spending more than earning) in September. Additionally, the IMF (International Monetary Fund - global lender that watches world economy and helps countries in crisis) has raised the growth forecast for FY27. According to the Free Press Journal, private sector activity also hit a four-month high in October as manufacturing and services gathered pace.

threads.title: Why Afghanistan's Neighbors Have Not Backed Pakistan's Strikes on the Taliban - The Diplomat - Asia-Pacific Current Affairs Magazine

events.headline: Why Afghanistan's Neighbors Have Not Backed Pakistan's Strikes on the Taliban - The Diplomat - Asia-Pacific Current Affairs Magazine
events.text: According to The Diplomat – Asia-Pacific Current Affairs Magazine, on October 5, Moscow hosted the eighth meeting of the special representatives and senior officials from regional countries for the Moscow Format to discuss political and economic relations with Afghanistan and counterterrorism and counter-narcotics cooperation. The Moscow Format includes Afghanistan, China, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan. But the meeting failed to adopt a joint statement because the Pakistani and Afghan delegates disagreed over the language on terrorism. The Taliban objected to the frequent mention of terrorism in reference to Afghanistan. Russia's special envoy for Afghanistan, Zamir Kabulov, said the Afghan delegates accepted similar language last year. events.text: According to India Sentinels, New Delhi: The defence ministry on Thursday signed two contracts worth about ₹4,106 crore to give the Indian Air Force (IAF) a dedicated communication satellite and to equip the Indian Navy with more Varunastra heavyweight torpedoes. The agreements were signed in New Delhi in the presence of the additional secretary and director general (acquisition), A Anbarasu. The larger of the two, valued at ₹2,563 crore, is for the GSAT (Geosynchronous Satellite - ISRO's series of communication satellites)-7C satellite. It was signed with NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), Bengaluru. The ₹1,543-crore contract for Varunastra torpedoes went to Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL), Hyderabad. Utkarsh Classes reported it as: "MoD (Ministry of Defence - runs India's armed forces) Signs ₹4,106 Crore Deals for GSAT-7C & Varunastra Torpedoes". UPDATE - 'Another institution being destroyed': Congress alleges RSS-BJP agenda behind Census 2027 changes
events.text: The Congress has accused the BJP (Bharatiya Janata Party - national political party, leads the NDA)-led Centre of pursuing a political agenda regarding Census 2027, as reported by The Times of India. This follows the government's amendment to the Census Rules 1990, which allows teachers from private institutions to be appointed as census officers. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh claims this expansion of eligible enumerators is a way to provide jobs for RSS and BJP workers. He linked this move to an RSS training camp and a high-level committee on demographic changes with members from the RSS ecosystem. Ramesh alleged that these developments could compromise the credibility of the census process. He further claimed that this action would contaminate an already subverted census.

events.headline: India's exports up 23% to $44.4 billion in Sep; trade deficit narrows to $30.21 billion
events.text: According to BusinessLine, Exports are maintaining their growth trend, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal said in a press briefing on trade data. India's exports increased by 23 per cent to USD 44.4 billion in September, and the trade deficit (shortfall; spending more than earning) narrowed to USD 30.21 billion, government data released on Thursday said. The country's imports rose by 8 per cent to $74.61 billion in September. India's trade deficit in September 2025 stood at USD 33 billion. During April-September this fiscal (related to government finances; 'this fiscal' means this financial year), exports jumped 18.51 per cent to USD 259.89 billion, and imports climbed 16.31 per cent to USD 437.53 billion. The Times of India reported it as: "Exports up 23%, trade deficit at $30 billion in September". Fast bowler Dilshan Madushanka led the charge with a career-best five-wicket haul before Kamindu Mendis anchored a comfortable chase, giving Sri Lanka a timely boost ahead of the title clash. The Russian president, wearing military uniform and speaking during a visit to a command post, said the operation was in response to Ukraine's 2024-25 incursion (sudden attack into enemy land) into Russia's western Kursk region. "The Russian armed forces were tasked not only with expelling the enemy from our land but also with establishing a security zone in the adjacent territory. This task is being carried out successfully," he said in televised comments on Friday. "Our goal is to ensure the absolute security of Russia's border regions for the future, and we do not plan to make this a subject for potential peace negotiations with Ukraine." - The planned security zone spanned 660km (410 miles), of which 70% was currently under Russia's control, Kremlin (Russia's presidential fortress in Moscow; means the Russian government) spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said. threads.title: India's services trade cushion faces pressure as imports outpace exports: ICICI Bank

events.headline: India's services trade cushion faces pressure as imports outpace exports: ICICI Bank
events.text: According to a research report by ICICI Bank, India's services trade surplus is facing pressure because services imports are growing faster than exports. This surplus traditionally helps compensate for the country's large merchandise trade deficit (shortfall; spending more than earning). However, net services exports declined 10 per cent year-on-year to 16.9 billion dollars in September 2026. This happened as gross services exports fell 0.9 per cent to around 36 billion dollars while services imports increased 8.9 per cent to approximately 19 billion dollars. This trend shows that India is spending more on overseas services than it is earning from selling services to foreign markets. Consequently, this growth in imports could reduce net foreign exchange earnings and weaken the cushion against the goods trade deficit.

events.headline: India's Services Trade Surplus Narrows 10% YoY to USD 16.9 Bn in Sept as Imports Outpace Exports: ICICI Bank
events.text: India's services trade surplus fell 10% to USD 16.9 Bn in September because imports rose 8.9% while exports fell 0.9%. This matters because it could pressure foreign exchange earnings that help offset India's merchandise trade deficit.

events.text: DD News reported that India's total exports grew by 4.22 per cent to USD 860.09 billion in the financial year 2025-26. This is an increase from USD 825.26 billion in the previous year. However, imports rose at a faster pace of 6.47 per cent to around USD 970 billion. This happened because merchandise imports rose sharply to USD 774.98 billion due to higher inbound shipments. As a result, the overall trade deficit (shortfall; spending more than earning) widened to USD 119.30 billion. This is higher than the deficit of USD 94.66 billion recorded in 2024-25.

threads.title: DA news: Assam, West Bengal, Telangana, Sikkim, Kerala - Check full list of states with dearness allowance hikes in 2026

events.headline: DA news: Assam, West Bengal, Telangana, Sikkim, Kerala - Check full list of states with dearness allowance hikes in 2026
events.text: Livemint reports that the government hikes dearness allowance biannually based on the 7th Central Pay Commission recommendations and All-India Consumer Price Index data. This allowance is a percentage of basic pay meant to reduce the impact of inflation (general rise in prices) and the rising cost of living. Over 1 crore beneficiaries, including 50 lakh central government employees and nearly 65 lakh pensioners, gain from these hikes. The Finance Ministry last increased the allowance from 58% to 60% of basic salary effective from 1 January 2026. While these announcements usually occur in March and October, the 8th CPC is now discussing further revisions. This commission is expected to submit its final recommendations by May 2027 at the latest.

events.headline: DA hike: Himachal Pradesh, Kerala, Telangana, Sikkim - Check full list of states with dearness allowance hikes this year
events.text: Livemint reports that several states including Himachal Pradesh, Kerala, Telangana, Sikkim, Punjab, and Andhra Pradesh have announced dearness allowance hikes this year. These updates are based on the 7th Central Pay Commission's recommendations using data from the All India Consumer Price Index. Such hikes benefit over 1 crore people, including 50 lakh central government employees and nearly 65 lakh pensioners. While these announcements usually happen in March and October, the government has not officially confirmed a date for the second hike this year. Consequently, employees and pensioners are now awaiting a possible 3-4% increase following the next meeting on 28 October.

threads.title: China's Q3 GDP Growth Rises To 4.5% as Strong Exports Boost Economic Recovery

events.headline: China's Q3 GDP Growth Rises To 4.5% as Strong Exports Boost Economic Recovery
events.text: Outlook India reports that China's economy grew by 4.5 percent year-on-year in the third quarter of 2026. This growth was supported by strong exports and industrial output, which rose 5.5 percent in September. The result is that the country has moved closer to its annual growth target of 4.5 to 5 percent. However, weak consumer spending and a prolonged property-sector slump continued to weigh on domestic demand. Because of this, the IMF (International Monetary Fund - global lender that watches world economy and helps countries in crisis) has called for stronger fiscal (related to government finances; 'this fiscal' means this financial year) support to boost domestic demand. This will help China sustain growth without relying so heavily on exports.

events.headline: TCS expands Indian Bank partnership, deploys BaNCS for Treasury in Sri Lanka
events.text: Tata Consultancy Services has expanded its partnership with Indian Bank to deploy TCS BaNCS for Treasury at the bank's Colombo branch in Sri Lanka. This move marks the company's entry into the country following successful deployments in India and GIFT City. TCS will help the bank modernise its overseas treasury operations across foreign exchange, investment management, and money markets. This transformation allows the Colombo branch to move to a single integrated platform for better risk controls and real-time visibility. As a result, the bank can reduce manual intervention and strengthen its regulatory readiness. TradingView, Machine Maker, and HDFC Sky reported this.

events.headline: TCS Extends Indian Bank Treasury Platform to Colombo, Marking Sri Lanka Entry
events.text: According to reports from Konsulteer, ANI (Asian News International - Indian news agency) News, and TradingView, TCS has entered Sri Lanka by extending its Indian Bank Treasury platform to Colombo. This entry happened as TCS BaNCS for Treasury was introduced through the Colombo branch of Indian Bank. This development comes while China pulls out of a 392 million dollar Sri Lanka port project. Such a move by China raises the question of whether this creates an opening for India in its own backyard. Consequently, India is expanding its financial technology presence in the neighbouring country.

threads.title: Indian Army to Get Its First Dedicated Communications Satellite GSAT-7B by Mid-2028

events.headline: Indian Army to Get Its First Dedicated Communications Satellite GSAT-7B by Mid-2028
events.text: According to SSBCrack, Defence.in, and Hindustan Times, the Indian Army will get its first dedicated communications satellite called GSAT (Geosynchronous Satellite - ISRO's series of communication satellites)-7B by mid-2028. This development addresses a long-standing requirement because the Army currently lacks its own satellite and relies on the Air Force's GSAT-7A. The five-tonne geostationary satellite will be launched by ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation - India's space agency) to provide secure and round-the-clock connectivity across challenging terrain and remote border areas. It is designed to support military operations and battlefield command and control by enabling beyond-line-of-sight communications for weapon systems, airborne platforms, and deployed troops. To achieve this, the Ministry of Defence signed a contract of approximately 3,000 crore rupees with NewSpace India Limited for its indigenous (made or developed in the country itself) design and manufacture.

events.headline: Sensex, Nifty crash: Why is stock market down today? Massive wealth eroded; investors lose ₹4 lakh crore
events.text: According to Livemint, DhanamOnline, and Univest, the Indian stock market suffered a strong sell-off on Monday, 19 October. The benchmark (standard used for comparison) indices, Sensex and Nifty 50, both dropped more than 1% due to weak global cues. This crash was driven by high Brent crude prices, which increased inflation (general rise in prices) and led to monetary tightening by central banks like the US (United States - country in North America; world's largest economy) Federal Reserve, Bank of Japan, and Reserve Bank of India. These factors raised concerns about economic growth and corporate profitability, while weak private banking and disappointing earnings further dragged the market. As a result, investors lost 4 lakh crore rupees in a single session. Following this significant drop, the NSE (National Stock Exchange - India's biggest stock exchange; runs the Nifty) and BSE (Bombay Stock Exchange - Asia's oldest stock exchange; runs the Sensex) will remain closed on October 20 for Dussehra.

threads.title: From Booking Courts to Building a Sports Ecosystem: How Hudle Is Scaling the Way India Plays

events.headline: From Booking Courts to Building a Sports Ecosystem: How Hudle Is Scaling the Way India Plays
events.text: Hudle began because finding and booking a place to play sports was harder than playing itself. At that time, sports venues were limited and not easily accessible to everyday players. To solve this, the sports-tech platform started by focusing on accessibility. According to Indian Startup Times, the company has now grown from a booking platform into a broader sports ecosystem. It now connects players with over 4,000 venues across 110-plus cities and supports more than 40 sports. The platform now includes venue operations, community building, player ratings, and AI (Artificial Intelligence - computers doing tasks that need human-like thinking)-powered match analysis.

events.text: As reported by the Indian Express, Vande Bharat Sleeper trains have started operating on the Varanasi-Delhi and Mumbai-Bengaluru routes. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw flagged off the Bengaluru-Mumbai train on Sunday and jointly flagged off the Varanasi-Delhi train with Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday. Both trains have 16 coaches and offer travel in First AC, Second AC, and Third AC classes. The Varanasi-New Delhi train will halt at Ghaziabad, Aligarh, Kanpur Central, and Prayagraj. This train operates daily except on Friday, while the return journey runs daily except on Saturday. Ticket fares for the Varanasi-New Delhi route range from Rs 1,915 for Third AC to Rs 3,030 for First AC.

The alliance between the two parties had previously broken down in September 2020 due to differences over three farm laws. Badal now identifies the Congress and the ruling Aam Aadmi Party as the principal rivals in the state. He stated that the Akali Dal is ready to work with parties that share its views for the betterment of Punjab. This comes after Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in August and Punjab Governor Gulab Chand Kataria. These developments have intensified speculation that the two former allies could come together again.

events.headline: Bangladesh's public debt ratio lower than those of India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka
events.text: Views Bangladesh and en.bd-pratidin.com report that Bangladesh has a public debt ratio lower than most South Asian countries. This is because its public debt as a share of gross domestic product is significantly lower than that of its neighbours. Based on International Monetary Fund estimates for 2026, Bangladesh's public debt is projected to be around 40 per cent of GDP. In comparison, the ratios for India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, the Maldives, Bhutan and Nepal are all considerably higher. For example, India's public debt could reach around 83 per cent of GDP in 2026. As a result, Bangladesh's public debt-to-GDP ratio is less than half that of India.

events.headline: ISRO to launch NVS-03 satellite as India looks to revive NavIC navigation system
ISRO to launch navigation satellite NVS-03 on Friday
events.text: According to Indian Express, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on Wednesday announced its next launch - the navigation satellite NVS-03 - on October 30 from Sriharikota. The NVS-03 is the third satellite in the next-generation navigation satellite system aimed at providing continuity of navigation services for the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS) series. The NVS-03 will carry onboard an indigenous (made or developed in the country itself) atomic clock along with other atomic clocks and satellite navigation signals that offer a wide coverage of the entire Indian landmass extending up to 1500 km. The NVS-03 weighs around 2,250 kg. It will be launched onboard the GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle - ISRO's heavy rocket)-F18 vehicle into the Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit. Instagram reported it as: "The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is set to launch its NVS-03 navigation satellite aboard the GSLV-F18 rocket from the Second Launch Pad at Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR), in Sriharikota on Friday, October 30, at 11:51 p.m., as p".

threads.title: DAC Clears Defence Acquisition Proposals Worth ₹2.12 Lakh Crore for Indian Army, Navy and Air Force

events.headline: DAC Clears Defence Acquisition Proposals Worth ₹2.12 Lakh Crore for Indian Army, Navy and Air Force
events.text: The Defence Acquisition Council, chaired by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, has approved capital acquisition proposals worth approximately ₹2.12 lakh crore for the Indian Army, Navy and Air Force. This move aims to boost military modernisation and indigenous (made or developed in the country itself) defence manufacturing. The approvals cover advanced equipment such as helicopters, artillery (large heavy guns) systems, air defence weapons, and various drone systems. To support the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative, about 82% of these procurements will come from Indian industry. Specifically, the Indian Army will receive high mobility vehicles and other critical systems to improve its combat preparedness and mobility. These updates were reported by SSBCrack, News On AIR and Defence Watch.

events.headline: Sarvam and Ministry of Defence sign framework for AI projects across the Indian Army, Navy and Air Force
events.text: According to India Technology News, a five-year MoU sets the route for AI adoption across the three Services and the joint organisations under HQ IDS, in step with India's push to build its own AI for defence. 28 October 2026, New Delhi: Sarvam has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS), Ministry of Defence, setting up an umbrella framework for AI projects across the Indian Army, the Indian Navy and the Indian Air Force. The framework also extends to the joint, tri-service and integrated organisations under HQ IDS. The MoU is a step in the Government's drive towards Atmanirbharta in defence, the indigenisation of defence equipment and capability that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has placed at the centre of national security. That same imperative now extends to artificial intelligence, which is becoming as consequential to military capability as the platforms it runs on. Building that capability in India, on Indian data and Indian compute, is the need of the hour.

events.headline: Sarvam Signs Five-Year MoU with Defence Ministry to Build AI for Army, Navy and Air Force
events.text: According to Convergence Now, India's artificial intelligence company Sarvam has signed a five-year memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Ministry of Defence to develop and deploy AI applications across the Indian Army, Navy and Air Force. The progress is part of the government's push to bring home-grown technology into military operations, training, and decision-making. The agreement, signed through Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS), also covers joint and integrated defence organisations. It will also provide post-deployment technical support, while HQ IDS will coordinate engagement across the participating organisations. The proposed applications will focus on decision support, target acquisition, and data fusion across the sensor-to-shooter loop, including collecting information, identifying potential targets, and passing relevant information to systems involved in responding to them. Sarvam AI reported it as: "Sarvam and Ministry of Defence sign AI MoU".

threads.title: China's Pursuit of Bangladesh Port Control Encounters Hurdles After Dhaka Engages Multiple Foreign Operators

events.headline: China's Pursuit of Bangladesh Port Control Encounters Hurdles After Dhaka Engages Multiple Foreign Operators
events.text: According to Defence.in, China's plan to gain control of seaports in Bangladesh to further its strategic interests in the Bay of Bengal has faced hurdles. While it was decided during Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's visit to Beijing that China would develop Mongla Port, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party government is awarding contracts to other global operators. To avoid total reliance on China, the interim (temporary) government signed agreements in 2025 for the development of Matarbari Port with Japan Overseas Cooperation Agency and the Ladia Container Terminal with the Maersk Group of Denmark. Specifically, the Chittagong Port Authority entered a 30 year agreement with the Maersk Group to design, finance, build and operate the Ladia Container Terminal. This shift shows that successive governments in Dhaka are involving multiple foreign players to modernise the country's ports.

They spent only a few hours on the island before leaving on Saturday night.

events.headline: U.P. Cabinet clears ₹1,947-cr textile park project, seven water-sewerage schemes in Lucknow, Varanasi
events.text: The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet approved Ramky Infrastructure Ltd as the preferred bidder to develop a PM (Prime Minister - head of the government) MITRA Mega Textile Park on the Lucknow-Hardoi border. Reported by The Hindu, the project will be built on 1,000 acres at an estimated cost of ₹1,947 crore. The Centre will provide financial assistance of up to 30 percent of the cost, with a maximum of ₹500 crore. This park aims to attract private investment and benefit exporters, garment manufacturers, and weavers. It is expected to generate direct and indirect employment for around one lakh people. Additionally, the Cabinet cleared expenditure proposals for seven drinking water and sewerage projects in Lucknow and Varanasi.

events.headline: Rubio to host G20 Foreign Ministers' meet in Atlanta on Oct 30-31
events.text: Secretary of State Marco Rubio will host the G20 (Group of Twenty - forum of 19 big economies plus the EU and the African Union) Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta on October 30-31. According to the U.S. Department of State, the meeting aims to strengthen practical cooperation on shared security and economic challenges. This event will set the stage for the leaders' meeting in December. The United States intends to return the G20 to its core mission of driving growth and strengthening economic security under President Trump's leadership. The U.S. will work with partners to address geopolitical crises that cause global economic shocks, such as threats to food security, energy, supply chains, and freedom of navigation. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar is scheduled to attend this meeting.

events.text: According to The Economic Times, the scheme seeks to promote domestic manufacturing by supporting the establishment of new facilities, expansion of existing units and development of testing infrastructure, skills and capacity across the container manufacturing value chain. This exposes container availability to global market fluctuations, freight volatility and supply-chain disruptions. China dominates global container production; Indian units face cost disadvantage China accounts for an estimated 90-97% of global shipping container manufacturing capacity, depending on the segment and year. Disruptions during the Covid pandemic, which led to container shortages and freight-rate volatility, further exposed the risks of relying heavily on imports for a critical component of international trade. Four components to support domestic manufacturing The scheme has four components: Interest Subvention Assistance, Testing and Certification Assistance, Land Leasing Support and Operational Expenditure (OPEX) Assistance.

threads.title: In a first since Operation Sindoor, India invites Pakistan to SCO meet in Delhi

events.headline: In a first since Operation Sindoor, India invites Pakistan to SCO meet in Delhi
events.text: According to Indian Express, this is the first such invitation by India to a senior minister of Pakistan ever since the military hostilities between the two countries in the wake of Operation Sindoor in May 2025 following the Pahalgam terror attack. The last time India hosted a senior minister of Pakistan was in May 2023 when Bilawal Bhutto, who was then the Foreign Minister of his country, travelled to Goa for a meeting of the SCO (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation - Eurasian security and economic group; India is a member) Foreign Ministers. The invitation to Pakistan's minister is part of Delhi's obligation to invite representatives from all SCO member countries since it had proposed to host the SCO civilisational dialogue forum. Pakistan is scheduled to host the summit of SCO leaders next year. For Delhi, the diplomatic task is cut out. Business Standard reported it as: "In a first after Op Sindoor, India invites Pakistan for SCO forum in Delhi". The 193-member General Assembly adopted the resolution on Wednesday, with 130 countries voting in favour, 17 against and 25 abstaining. Delivering India's statement, Counsellor at India's Permanent Mission to the UN (world body of 193 countries for peace and cooperation) Soumya Nair said the General Assembly has repeatedly called for an end to the embargo and rejected laws and regulations with extraterritorial effects that adversely affect the sovereignty (full power of a country to govern itself) of other states and the progress and prosperity of their peoples. "India reiterates the Assembly's call to all states to refrain from promulgating and applying, and to repeal and invalidate, such laws and measures in conformity with their obligations under the Charter of the United Nations and international law," she said.

events.text: According to Times of India, BJP (Bharatiya Janata Party - national political party, leads the NDA)'s big win in MLC elections comes with setbacks in Nagpur and Varanasi The MLC elections across four states brought both shock and cheer for the BJP and Congress. While the Congress suffered a humiliating defeat in Karnataka, where it is in power but failed to win a single seat, the BJP faltered in two constituencies which mattered the most. One being Nagpur, which is home to the RSS headquarters, and Varanasi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi's parliamentary constituency.The BJP nevertheless emerged as the largest party, winning 13 of the 28 seats contested, while its allies took the NDA (National Democratic Alliance - BJP-led ruling alliance (also: National Defence Academy))'s tally to 16. The alliance swept all four seats in Karnataka, won six of the 11 seats in Uttar Pradesh and secured four of the eight seats in Bihar. In Maharashtra, the ruling Mahayuti won two of the five seats, while the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi secured three.The Congress's only victory came from Nagpur, a political stronghold of Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and Union minister Nitin Gadkari.

threads.title: Afghanistan opium production jumps fivefold as farmers find ways round Taliban ban

events.headline: Afghanistan opium production jumps fivefold as farmers find ways round Taliban ban
events.text: According to UN (world body of 193 countries for peace and cooperation) News, Afghanistan opium production jumps fivefold as farmers find ways round Taliban ban Opium production in Afghanistan has risen fivefold in a year. According to a UN survey released on Thursday, it's the first significant increase since the Taliban banned poppy cultivation in 2022. The UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) found that the area planted with opium poppy grew by 330 per cent, to more than 43,000 hectares, up from about 10,000 hectares in 2025. Estimated production rose by 400 per cent, from about 300 tonnes to just under 1,500 tonnes. Both figures remain well below levels before the ban, when some 232,000 hectares were under cultivation. Afghanistan International reported it as: "Opium Production In Afghanistan Has Increased Fivefold, Says UN". In related news, Indian Aviation News Net reported: Indian nationals arrested in Sri Lanka, Nepal in separate drug trafficking cases.

events.headline: Afghanistan opium poppy cultivation surges despite Taliban government ban: UN

events.headline: ISRO schedules launch of 3rd indigenous navigation satellite on October 30

The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is set to launch its NVS-03 navigation satellite aboard the GSLV-F18 rocket from the Second Launch Pad at Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR), in Sriharikota on Friday, October 30, at 11:51 p.m., as p
events.text: Instagram reports that the Indian Space Research Organisation is set to launch the NVS-03 navigation satellite. This key swadeshi GPS satellite will be carried aboard the GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle - ISRO's heavy rocket)-F18 rocket. The launch is scheduled for Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:51 p.m. It will lift off from the second launch pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota. The countdown is currently progressing for this crucial mission.

events.headline: GSLV places next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03 into orbit
ISRO successfully launches 3rd-generation navigation satellite NVS-03
events.text: Greater Kashmir and Startup Pedia report that ISRO successfully launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Andhra Pradesh. The satellite was carried by the GSLV-F18 rocket to strengthen India's indigenous navigation system called NavIC. This mission was the 20th flight of the GSLV and was completed with the shortest turnaround time of 56 days between two launches. The NVS-03 satellite carries an indigenous atomic clock and adds the L1 frequency band to improve positioning and timing capabilities. As a result, the 2,232-kg satellite was placed in its intended Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit. The ISRO chief stated that two more navigation satellites are to be launched.

events.headline: Aid Mission Set to Enter Oleshky as a Localized Russia-Ukraine Truce Holds for a Third Day
events.text: According to U.S. News & World Report, Aid mission set to enter Oleshky as a localized Russia-Ukraine truce (temporary stop to fighting) holds for a third day Humanitarian (related to helping people in need) aid is set to arrive in Oleshky, Ukraine, on Friday as a localized ceasefire (agreement to stop fighting) between Russia and Ukraine continues for a third day KHERSON, Ukraine -- Humanitarian aid is poised to roll into the stricken city of Oleshky on Friday, a Ukrainian official said, as a localized ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine stretched into a third day and military units cleared away landmines. Moscow and Kyiv have observed the truce in and around the devastated southern Ukrainian city since Tuesday, despite remaining locked in war since Russia's all-out invasion of its neighbor more than 4 ½ years ago. Previous efforts to secure ceasefires either never worked out or the truces quickly fell apart. But elsewhere, a jet-powered Russian drone hit two trains stopped at a station in central Ukraine, killing at least 13 people and injuring 10 others, officials said.

events.headline: World Must Triple Nature Restoration to Meet 2030 Goal, UN Report Tells Biodiversity Summit
events.text: Health Policy Watch reports that a new United Nations report warns the world must triple its nature restoration pace to meet 2030 goals. This is because the destruction of forests, farmland, wilderness, and waterways is still outpacing restoration efforts worldwide. To fix this, annual spending on restoration would need to rise more than fourfold from 64 billion dollars in 2022 to 296 billion dollars by 2030. The assessment was released in Yerevan, Armenia, a day before the COP17 biodiversity summit closes. This report is the first to tally restoration efforts across the world's oceans, freshwater systems, and land masses.

events.headline: Election Commission extends SIR timelines in Maharashtra, Delhi, Andhra, Haryana, Telangana & Nagaland
events.text: According to Revoi.in and Singrauli Mirror, the Election Commission of India has revised the schedule for the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. This change affects Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Telangana, Nagaland, and the Union Territory of Delhi. The timelines were extended following requests from the concerned chief electoral officers. In Maharashtra, the deadline for filing claims and objections is now November 13 instead of October 26. The notice phase and disposal of claims will continue until November 25. Consequently, the final roll in Maharashtra will be published on November 30.

threads.title: Supreme Court Upholds War Injury Pension for Indian Army Soldier Disabled During Kargil Operation Rakshak, Rejects Defence Ministry's Narrow Interpretation of Specially Notified Operations

events.headline: Supreme Court Upholds War Injury Pension for Indian Army Soldier Disabled During Kargil Operation Rakshak, Rejects Defence Ministry's Narrow Interpretation of Specially Notified Operations
events.text: Raw Law reports that the Supreme Court upheld the War Injury Pension for an Indian Army soldier disabled during Operation Rakshak in Kargil. Narender Kumar developed rheumatoid arthritis and spinal conditions while serving from July 2003 to July 2005. The Defence Ministry argued that Operation Rakshak was not a qualifying specially notified operation for this higher pension. However, the court rejected this narrow interpretation and ruled that the operation is covered by the policy. This decision follows previous successes for the soldier before the Armed Forces Tribunal and the High Court. The court dismissed the Union appeal and called for clearer government notifications regarding pension entitlements.

events.headline: "Congress keep losing elections, yet have audacity to shift blame onto EVM, ECI": BJP MLA Ram Kadam after MLC poll results
events.text: According to India Gazette, BJP (Bharatiya Janata Party - national political party, leads the NDA) MLA (Member of Legislative Assembly - elected member of a state assembly) Ram Kadam criticised the Congress party following the recent MLC election results. He stated that Congress continues to blame the Election Commission of India and Electronic Voting Machines for its losses. Kadam pointed out that the elections were actually conducted using paper ballots. Despite this, Congress won only one out of 28 seats in Maharashtra by a narrow margin and secured no seats in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, or Karnataka. He argued that the party should introspect on its defeats instead of blaming the electoral process. He concluded by asking if the Congress would finally accept reality.

events.text: WION reports that External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar arrived in Atlanta, US (United States - country in North America; world's largest economy), for a two-day G20 (Group of Twenty - forum of 19 big economies plus the EU and the African Union) Foreign Ministers' meeting from October 30 to 31, 2026. The US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is hosting the event, which was convened by the US Department of State. The talks focus on the G20's economic mission, economic security, supply chains, and major geopolitical crises like the Middle East and Ukraine. These discussions also cover energy, food security, and freedom of navigation, which are critical for India's fertiliser, LNG, and oil imports. Additionally, Jaishankar will attend a Quad foreign ministers' meeting on the sidelines of the G20 event.

threads.title: Cabinet approves Rs 100 billion scheme to boost container manufacturing

events.headline: Cabinet approves Rs 100 billion scheme to boost container manufacturing
events.text: The Union Cabinet has approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme with an outlay of Rs 100 billion through 2039-40. Reported by Indian Infrastructure Magazine, this scheme was announced in the Union Budget 2026-27 to establish a globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem in India. It will support new manufacturing facilities and the expansion of existing units to increase annual domestic capacity from around 70,000 TEUs to 750,000 TEUs. The funds include Rs 88.91 billion for operational expenditure assistance, Rs 8.59 billion for interest subsidies, and Rs 1.5 billion for testing and certification facilities. This move is expected to reduce import dependence and strengthen maritime (related to the sea) supply-chain resilience. Additionally, it aims to generate 3,000 direct and over 50,000 indirect jobs.

events.text: G20 (Group of Twenty - forum of 19 big economies plus the EU and the African Union) foreign ministers will end their two days of talks in Atlanta on October 31, 2026, without reaching consensus on critical global security issues. According to The Hindu, LawStreet Journal, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan, divisions over Russia's war with Ukraine overshadowed the meeting. Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski noted that it is difficult to agree on a common line when participants in ongoing wars are around the table. Because of this, the group will not release a joint communique. Instead, US (United States - country in North America; world's largest economy) Secretary of State Marco Rubio will release a chairman's statement summarising the talks. Rubio also cancelled the traditional group photograph after European diplomats threatened to boycott it over the inclusion of Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.
sources: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan

events.headline: G20 Foreign Ministers Fail To Reach Consensus At Atlanta Meeting Amid Global Security Disputes

events.text: According to reports by whispersinthecorridors.net, nationpathindia.com, and defence.newsd.in, Air Marshal Inderpal Singh Walia has been appointed as the new Vice Chief of the Air Staff of the Indian Air Force. He will take over this role with effect from November 1, 2026. He is currently the Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Eastern Air Command and an alumnus of the National Defence Academy. Commissioned in the Fighter stream on June 11, 1988, he is qualified on all variants of the MiG-21, MiG-23, MiG-27, Jaguar, and Su-30 MKI. Over a career of almost four decades, he has held various command and staff appointments, including commanding a frontline fighter squadron and the Tactics and Air Combat Development Establishment.

threads.title: Heat stress could cost Sri Lanka and the Maldives the equivalent of 147,000 full-time jobs by 2040

events.headline: Heat stress could cost Sri Lanka and the Maldives the equivalent of 147,000 full-time jobs by 2040
events.text: According to studies by the International Labour Organization, rising temperatures and workplace heat stress are already affecting workers and economies in Sri Lanka and the Maldives. This heat stress caused additional losses of working time and GDP (Gross Domestic Product - total value of goods and services produced in a country) in both countries in 2023. These economic and employment consequences are expected to intensify substantially in the coming decades. By 2040, reduced working time could cost the two nations the equivalent of around 147,000 full-time jobs. Even under a low-emissions pathway, this could lead to combined annual GDP losses of around US (United States - country in North America; world's largest economy)$26.6 billion. These projections include approximately 145,000 lost jobs and US$26 billion in GDP losses for Sri Lanka, while the Maldives could lose 2,400 jobs and US$576 million in GDP.

threads.title: Launch of NVS-03: PM Modi congratulates scientists, engineers at ISRO

events.headline: Launch of NVS-03: PM Modi congratulates scientists, engineers at ISRO
events.text: According to PM India, Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation - India's space agency) scientists and engineers on the successful launch of GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle - ISRO's heavy rocket)-F18 carrying NVS-03 on October 31, 2026. This mission was conducted to strengthen NavIC, which is the indigenous (made or developed in the country itself) satellite navigation system of India. The NVS-03 satellite was placed into the designated injection orbit by a GSLV rocket. As a result, India's independent regional navigation satellite system was restored to its minimum operational configuration of four satellites on October 30, 2026. The Prime Minister stated that the enhanced capabilities of NVS-03 will support navigation services for the people and further India's pursuit of self-reliance in critical technologies.

threads.title: Can Tamil Be Used in Madras High Court? Advocates' Association Challenges 1965 Cabinet Decision

events.headline: Can Tamil Be Used in Madras High Court? Advocates' Association Challenges 1965 Cabinet Decision
events.text: The Madras High Court Advocates Association has challenged a 1965 Union Cabinet decision that kept English as the common language in the Supreme Court and High Courts. According to reports by NDTV Profit, Live Law, and The Hindu, the Association argues that this decision makes Article 348(2) of the Constitution a dead letter. They claim that while Hindi speaking states were permitted to use Hindi, proposals from non-Hindi speaking states to use regional languages were rejected. The Association believes the cabinet decision goes against the Constitution which permits other languages for official state purposes. A bench of Chief Justice SA Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan was informed that a similar plea was filed in Madurai. Consequently, the court has adjourned the plea to next week.

events.text: Livemint reports that the Securities and Exchange Board of India has recommended removing the long-term capital gains tax for foreign investors. This suggestion comes as foreign investors have already withdrawn over ₹2.34 lakh crore from the Indian stock market in 2026. Currently, these investors pay a 12.5% tax on eligible equity investments held for more than 12 months. SEBI has also proposed tax relief for domestic mutual fund investors when they sell existing holdings to invest in new ones. These developments occur while the Sensex and Nifty have seen significant rallies. This move aims to address the sustained outflows of foreign capital from the market.

events.headline: Imports, low base power fastest GST growth in four years in October
events.text: Mint reported that India's gross GST collections grew by 22.9 percent year-on-year to ₹2.31 trillion in October. This is the fastest growth recorded in four years since September 2022. The increase was driven by a 42.2 percent surge in import-related revenue and a low statistical base from last October. Domestic GST collections also grew 15.8 percent to ₹1.59 trillion. This result marks a sharp acceleration from the 4.6 percent growth seen in October last year.

events.text: The Hindu reported that Pakistan has warned Afghanistan that it will take all necessary measures to eliminate cross-border terror threats. This follows remarks by Afghan Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, who accused Pakistan of lacking readiness for a peaceful resolution and having wrong policies. In response, Pakistan's Ministry of Information and Broadcasting accused the Taliban leadership of refusing to address militancy from Afghan soil. The ministry stated that the regime is shifting blame on Islamabad and has a misguided approach to the root cause of deteriorating relations. Pakistan asserted that its national security cannot be held hostage to the inaction of the Taliban regime. Consequently, Pakistan declared that terrorism is a red line and the security of its citizens is non-negotiable.

events.headline: At G20 foreign ministers' meet: Jaishankar raises energy crisis, flags sanctions, attacks
events.text: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar raised concerns about the global energy crisis at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, US. He stated that the crisis is caused by unpredictability, disruption, and unaffordable costs rather than a lack of production. According to The Indian Express, Jaishankar flagged that sanctions, obstacles, and deliberate attacks on energy infrastructure are a calculated strategy to hold prices hostage. He noted that these actions show little regard for the predicament of low-income countries. These remarks come amid US sanctions on Iranian oil and attacks on energy ships in the Russia-Ukraine and West Asia wars. The Atlanta talks eventually ended without a consensus on key global security issues.

events.text: According to The Hindu, Al Jazeera, and Al Arabiya English, cyber attacks hit the emergency and air raid alert systems of Russia and Ukraine. These attacks occurred after the longest truce of the war ended on Sunday, November 1, 2026, because Russia refused an extension. Ukraine suspected its system was compromised after baseless radiation threat alerts appeared. Later, Russia reported a massive cyberattack where hackers posted false information on its emergency warnings app. Ukraine blamed Russia for its hack, but neither government has confirmed who was responsible for the attacks. This rare pause in fighting had previously enabled a humanitarian mission to the city of Oleshky.
